description: Import HISTORICAL purchase orders (already received in a previous system). receivedDate − orderDate becomes the OBSERVED LEAD TIME the reorder engine reads (POs from the last 12 months count; it needs at least 3 per item to beat the vendor default), so spread real dates rather than inventing them. Also seeds the purchasing graph: vendors are created by name (new ones get a default lead time from the batch average), unknown items are created costed from their PO line, ItemSupplier vendor-terms links (with MOQ) are created per (item, vendor) pair, and items without a default vendor get one. Never touches inventory — use set_inventory_levels for opening stock. Idempotent: POs whose number already exists are skipped, so retrying or chunking is safe. Max 500 orders per call. Operator (unpinned) credentials on 3PL tenants pass clientId to name the client the history belongs to. Requires the governed two-step protocol: call with preview=true to validate and receive a parse report (PO count, would-create counts, sample) plus a single-use previewReceipt, then repeat the identical call with that previewReceipt and a fresh idempotencyKey to commit — a bare call is refused with PREVIEW_RECEIPT_REQUIRED.

clientId.description: Operator (unpinned) credentials on 3PL tenants: the target client id (GUID) the imported history belongs to — get ids from list_clients. Client-pinned credentials omit this; the credential decides.

createMissingItems.description: Create items that the POs reference but the tenant doesn't have yet (default true). Vendors and vendor links are always seeded.

idempotencyKey.description: Caller-generated idempotency key; required with previewReceipt to commit.

orders.description: The historical purchase orders to import (max 500 per call).

expectedDate.description: Expected delivery date (ISO 8601). Persisted as the PO's due date; distinct from receivedDate (when goods actually arrived).

expenses.description: Optional order-level expenses (freight, tax, duty, etc.). Each expense becomes an expense-typed line on the PO and is allocated proportionally by value across the goods lines to populate per-line Expense fields.

category.description: REQUIRED. Expense category code — one of: tax, shipping, tariffs, freight, broker_fee, drayage, demurrage, exam, duty, other.

name.description: Optional display name for the expense line (defaults to the category label).

internalNote.description: Internal/private note on the purchase order (defaults to Note when omitted).

lines.description: Order lines. At least one required.

expense.description: Per-line freight/landed-cost expense amount. For CSVs that embed a freight column per line rather than as a separate order-level charge. Written directly to the goods line's Expense field; included in the landed unit cost: (UnitCost + Expense/Qty).

itemName.description: Item display name; resolves the line only when it has no SKU or UPC, and names the item when it has to be created.

minimumOrderQuantity.description: This supplier's minimum order quantity for the item — stored on the ItemSupplier vendor-terms link (created if missing; an existing link only gains a MOQ it didn't have).

sku.description: Item SKU. A line with a SKU resolves on it alone (case-insensitive); an unknown SKU is a new item, even when its UPC or name is known.

unitCost.description: Historical unit cost — recorded verbatim on the line; also seeds the item's cost when the item is created by this import. Null or omitted means no cost recorded.

uom.description: Unit of measure name; find-or-create, only used when creating the item.

upc.description: Item UPC/barcode (exact match), used to resolve the line only when it has no SKU. A new SKU whose UPC already belongs to another item cannot be created.

note.description: Public-facing note on the purchase order.

orderDate.description: REQUIRED. When the PO was placed (ISO 8601). A value with a Z or offset is that instant; a bare date is that calendar day in the tenant's time zone (bound to local noon); receivedDate and expectedDate are read the same way.

poNumber.description: REQUIRED. The source system's PO number — used verbatim (no renumbering) and as the idempotent dedup identity.

receivedDate.description: When the goods arrived (ISO 8601). receivedDate − orderDate is the observed lead time that feeds reorder points. Omit for open/in-flight POs — they contribute to on-order quantity but not lead-time observation.

status.description: PO lifecycle status: open, received, partiallyReceived, cancelled. Defaults to 'received' when receivedDate is present, 'open' when absent. Cancelled POs are imported for audit completeness but excluded from both lead-time observation and inbound quantity.

supplierName.description: REQUIRED. Supplier name; the supplier is created if the tenant doesn't have it.

preview.description: Step 1 of the required two-step write: set true to validate and receive a structured preview plus a single-use previewReceipt. Nothing is imported until the commit call.

previewReceipt.description: Step 2 of the required two-step write: the receipt returned by the preview call. Supply together with a fresh idempotencyKey to commit; calls without it are refused.

supplierAliases.description: Optional vendor-name aliases to resolve spelling inconsistencies before import. Keys are variant names found in the data, values are the canonical name to use. Preview surfaces vendorCollisions — use them to build this map, then re-preview or commit with the aliases applied.

warehouseId.description: Optional destination warehouse id (GUID); left unset on the imported POs when omitted (lead-time math does not use it).

name: import_historical_purchase_orders
title: Import Historical Purchase Orders
